dedupe_keys.name: global food security index gfsi economist impact affordability availability quality and resilience of food systems in 113 countries

description: The Global Food Security Index scores the food security environment of 113 countries on a common framework, produced by Economist Impact. It groups indicators into four pillars: affordability, covering consumers' ability to buy food, vulnerability to price shocks and safety nets; availability, covering agricultural production, the risk of supply disruption, national capacity to distribute food and research; quality and safety, covering diet diversity, nutrition and food safety; and sustainability and adaptation, covering exposure to climate change, natural resource risks and adaptation. The 2022 edition, the eleventh, found food environments deteriorating for a third year. Coverage is 113 countries with annual editions from 2012 to 2022. Country scores and rankings are free to explore and the index can be downloaded from the website, with methodology documents. Caveats: it is a composite index built on weightings the producer chose, some indicators are qualitative expert scores, editions revise earlier data, and no edition has appeared since 2022. Simulation uses: ranking countries by vulnerability to food supply disruption, weighting food import dependence in trade shock models, and comparing distribution infrastructure readiness. Related records: the IFPRI Food Security Portal (data-ifpri-food-security-portal) monitors prices and trade restrictions and the IPC country data (data-ipc-acute-food-insecurity-country-data) measure acute food insecurity.
